texts.text: Weather Report

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Scattered rains brought variable precipitation accumulations across Manitoba. Most regions received more than 6 mm of rain. Parts of the Interlake, Southwest, and Eastern regions received 15 - 40 mm. The highest accumulation of precipitation in the past seven days was at Bede with 54.2 mm.
texts.text: Scattered rains brought variable precipitation accumulations across Manitoba. Most regions received more than 6 mm of rain. Parts of the Interlake, Southwest, and Eastern regions received 15 - 40 mm. The highest accumulation of precipitation in the past seven days was at Bede with 54.2 mm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to September 13 range from 236 mm to 365 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Since May 1, large areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have accumulated more than 300 mm of precipitation. Seasonal accumulations are above normal for the majority of the Northwest and Southwest regions. Large areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have seen accumulations over 120% of normal. A few localized areas of the Interlake, Central and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 90% of the 30-year average.

texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Producers were back in the field late last week and over the weekend. Dewey mornings and tough conditions in the evening resulted in shorter harvest days. Producers are having to deal with wet field conditions, with some combines and grain carts getting stuck, due to last week's heavy rains. A light frost occurred in most areas on Sunday morning, with temperatures dipping to 0°C for a few hours. Little to no crop damage has been observed. Grain drying and aeration are happening on many farms. Rain at the start of this week will further delay harvest.

A light frost occurred in most areas on Sunday morning, with temperatures dipping to 0°C for a few hours. Little to no crop damage has been observed. Grain drying and aeration are happening on many farms. Rain at the start of this week will further delay harvest.

texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Mixed weather this week allowed for some harvest progress. Warm temperatures allowed for drying conditions across most of the region. While some progress was made throughout the week in fields that were dry enough, most operations were able to get going over the weekend. Heavy dews have been a challenge, narrowing the harvest window. Overnight temperatures below zero were reported at two weather stations over the past week. Some post-harvest field operations have occurred where conditions are dry enough.

texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field operations resumed by the middle to end of last week. Wet weather combined with cool nights, and heavy dews has delayed harvest for many. Fall activities such as baling, harrowing, cultivating and ditching are well underway.
texts.text: Field operations resumed by the middle to end of last week. Wet weather combined with cool nights, and heavy dews has delayed harvest for many. Fall activities such as baling, harrowing, cultivating and ditching are well underway.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Spring cereal harvest is nearing completion. Much of the harvested grain requires additional drying or aeration. Some remaining spring cereals are lodged. Spring wheat yields and protein range from average to good. Barley yields are slightly above average. Oat test weights are lower than typical, likely due to lower soil moisture during critical development stages. Spring cereals that were harvested later in the season have seen quality declines, and there have been some pre-harvest sprouting issues.

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans are at R7 (beginning maturity) and approaching R8. Due to dry and warm conditions earlier in the season, many plants have predominantly two-seeded pods, with few four-seeded pods. Pod abortion has also occurred in the upper canopy in many fields. Later-maturing varieties or late planted crops may see some improved pod-fill from the recent rainfall.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest and swathing continue. More canola is being swathed this year than in recent years, likely due to increasing levels of verticillium stripe. Pre-harvest sprouting has been an issue in some fields. In general, yields have been lower than in recent years. Pod shattering and drop has been a common issue due to strong winds.
